key_insight: Nitrogen reduction activity in intermetallic catalysts is governed not only by the d-band center, but also strongly by s- and p-band descriptors and local charge effects.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster screening of non-noble NRR catalysts using lightweight ML models built on physically meaningful electronic descriptors.
method: Built a dataset of 47 bimetallic intermetallic compounds and ~1,200 adsorption-energy data points for N2, N2H, and NH3.
Trained ML models using intrinsic material properties, band centers/fillings, and neighboring-atom Bader charges.
Used SHAP analysis to identify which descriptors most influence adsorption strength.
evidence_signal: The models achieved mean absolute errors of 0.26 eV for N2, 0.39 eV for N2H, and 0.17 eV for NH3 using only 20 key features.
watch_item: The study is limited to a specific 47-IMC dataset, so descriptor transferability to broader catalyst families and more complex surfaces still needs validation.
paper_title: Going Beyond the d-band Center to Design Intermetallic Catalysts for Nitrogen Reduction: A High-Throughput DFT and Machine Learning Study
